title: SQL on FHIR benchmark hook manifest schema
description: Declarative manifest describing a benchmark hook: EXACTLY ONE lifecycle mode — `command` (spawn mode: the harness starts the hook service with an assigned HOOK_PORT and owns termination), `endpoint` (connect mode: an operator-managed hook service the harness only connects to), or `cli` (CLI mode: an argv template the harness spawns fresh per run; no service, no implementation-side code) — plus the STATIC identity of the implementation under test. The harness copies `implementation` into the emitted report verbatim. The hook protocol itself (JSON over local HTTP) is specified in the benchmark-hook-format capability.

command.description: Spawn mode: argv array to start the hook service; the first element is the executable. Resolved relative to `cwd`. The harness passes the port to listen on as the HOOK_PORT environment variable.

endpoint.description: Connect mode: localhost base URL of an operator-managed hook service (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8095). The harness only connects; it never sends shutdown and never terminates the service.

run.description: CLI mode: argv template spawned fresh per run (first element is the executable; no shell). The placeholders {dataDir}, {viewFile} and {outCsv} are substituted as substrings within each element; the template must use {outCsv}.

cli.description: CLI mode: a stateless command-line hook described entirely by an argv template. The harness synthesizes the capabilities handshake (end_to_end only) and spawns one fresh engine process per run.

cwd.description: Spawn mode: working directory for the hook service. A relative path is resolved against the manifest file's own directory (the default).

env.description: Spawn mode: extra environment variables for the hook process, merged over the harness's environment.

implementation.description: Static identity of the implementation under test, in the report format's structured shape; copied verbatim into the report's `implementation`.
